item.title: Your menu doesn’t need Miller’s 7±2 rule
item.content:encoded: Miller’s 7±2 rule was about memory, not how many elements you can put on the screen. Learn why it doesn’t apply to menu items and what UX designers should take from the original research.

item.title: Pixels of the Week – February 22, 2026
item.content:encoded: This edition looks at AI hype pressure in design and dev work and why chatbot-first UX often fails. Also: an amazing pink moth, embroidery insect art inspiration and a reminder to use prefers-reduced-motion for your animations.

item.title: Pixels of the Week – February 15, 2026
item.content:encoded: This edition explores how accessibility innovations became mainstream, 5 quick component checks to build better UI and invisible work in projects. Also: open source design tools, UI inspiration and new CSS features in 2026.

item.title: Pixels of the Week – February 8, 2026
item.content:encoded: This week we dive into how the same UI is perceived differently for disabled users, how sound can improve UX, and how to choose the right list form controls. Also: data-viz inspiration, accessibility patterns, and a few brain-bending curiosities.

item.title: Pixels of the Week – February 1, 2026

item.title: Pixels of the Week – January 25, 2026
item.content:encoded: This week we explore the new confusing macOS icons, why humanity over automation is a competition advantage, and red flags for soul-crushing jobs. Plus, death to scroll fade animations, a giant BIC lamp, a fun LinkedIn job title maxximizer, etc.

item.title: Pixels of the Week – January 18, 2026
item.content:encoded: A fun API to say "no" with different excuses, Instagram’s failure on video accessibility, and why we shouldn’t humanize AI. Also: Microsoft's Fluent UI resources for designers, cute animated icons, and creepy cute cozy game vibes.

item.title: Pixels of the Week – January 11, 2026
